query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved wear resistance and low friction coefficients. Various studies have explored the effects of different alloying elements, processing routes, and microstructural features on the tribological properties of HEAs. Recent studies have shown that HEAs with nanohierarchical architecture and composition undulation can exhibit remarkable wear resistance and low friction coefficients. Additionally, the use of surface engineering techniques, such as electroless copper plating, can enhance the interfacial bonding and properties of HEA-based composites.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in developing HEAs with improved tribological properties, there is still a need to overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range (room temperature to 800 °C).
decision.why: This approach has shown promise in recent studies, such as PMC10241162, where a Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 complex concentrated alloy with nanohierarchical architecture and composition undulation exhibited ultralow wear rate and low friction coefficient.
